Topics · The holy books together

Does God want sacrifices, or a good heart?

Micah names justice, mercy, humility. The Quran asks what of an offering reaches God, and what a steward owes.

Part 1 of 4

﴿لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَـٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Their meat will not reach Allāh, nor will their blood, but what reaches Him is piety from you. Thus have We subjected them to you that you may glorify Allāh for that [to] which He has guided you; and give good tidings to the doers of good.

Quran · Al-Hajj 22:37

Translation

If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it. Will I eat the meat of bulls, or drink the blood of goats? Offer to God the sacrifice of thanksgiving. Pay your vows to the Most High.

Original · Hebrew

אִם־אֶ֭רְעַב לֹא־אֹ֣מַר לָ֑ךְ כִּי־לִ֥י תֵ֝בֵ֗ל וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃ הַֽ֭אוֹכַל בְּשַׂ֣ר אַבִּירִ֑ים וְדַ֖ם עַתּוּדִ֣ים אֶשְׁתֶּֽה׃ זְבַ֣ח לֵאלֹהִ֣ים תּוֹדָ֑ה וְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְעֶלְי֣וֹן נְדָרֶֽיךָ׃

the Psalms · 50:12-14

World English Bible

Micah asks what a person should bring before God: rams, rivers of oil, even a firstborn? His answer names no altar: justice, love of mercy, walking humbly with your God. He is not cancelling the Temple, whose offerings the Torah commands and whose loss Jews have mourned for centuries. He is saying what it was for. The verse makes the same move as plainly: neither flesh nor blood reaches God. What reaches Him is the reverence of the one who brings them.

A question for you

When Micah leaves the Temple out, what do you think he is doing?

If you sayHe assumes it, and names what must go with it
ThenMany Jewish readers take it so. It means the Temple's service was never meant to stand alone. The verse says the same of offerings.
If you sayHe says justice matters more than sacrifice
ThenThe Talmud reports a sage saying something close: that righteous giving outweighs all the offerings. If that order holds, it holds in an age without a Temple too.
If you sayHe warns against using ritual to avoid justice
ThenThen his words apply in any age and to any practice: prayer, charity, pilgrimage. The Quran speaks to its own readers the same way.

Part 2 of 4

﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱلْإِحْسَـٰنِ وَإِيتَآئِ ذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَيَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ وَٱلْبَغْىِ ۚ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, Allāh orders justice and good conduct and giving [help] to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:90

Translation

Therefore turn to your God. Keep kindness and justice, and wait continually for your God.

Original · Hebrew

וְאַתָּ֖ה בֵּאלֹהֶ֣יךָ תָשׁ֑וּב חֶ֤סֶד וּמִשְׁפָּט֙ שְׁמֹ֔ר וְקַוֵּ֥ה אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תָּמִֽיד׃

Hosea · 12:6

World English Bible

What, then, is required? The verse's list opens as Micah's does: justice and kindness. Its word ihsan, doing a thing as beautifully as it can be done, stands near the Hebrew hesed. It adds giving to those close to you, and forbids indecency, wrong and oppression. No building appears here either. A person could keep all of it on a day when every sanctuary on earth was closed.

A question for you

Compare Micah's list with the verse's. What do you notice?

If you sayWalking humbly is missing from the verse
ThenA careful catch. The Quran has a line on that, very close to Micah's own image, and it comes next.
If you sayGiving to kin is missing from Micah
ThenMicah speaks briefly, and the Torah fills in the detail about kin, the poor and the stranger. What seems missing here stands in the same book.
If you sayThey are very nearly the same
ThenThen two voices, in two tongues and two ages, give one answer. Ask what would explain that.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلْجَـٰهِلُونَ قَالُوا۟ سَلَـٰمًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily,[1035] and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace,[1036]

Translator's notes

[1035] i.e., gently, with dignity but without arrogance. [1036] Or "safety," i.e., words free from fault or evil.

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:63

Translation

He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

Original · Hebrew

הִגִּ֥יד לְךָ֛ אָדָ֖ם מַה־טּ֑וֹב וּמָֽה־יְהוָ֞ה דּוֹרֵ֣שׁ מִמְּךָ֗ כִּ֣י אִם־עֲשׂ֤וֹת מִשְׁפָּט֙ וְאַ֣הֲבַת חֶ֔סֶד וְהַצְנֵ֥עַ לֶ֖כֶת עִם־אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

Micah · 6:8

World English Bible

Micah's third phrase is the quiet one: walk humbly with your God. The verse describes God's servants by the way they walk: lightly on the earth, answering rudeness with peace. Both use a person's walk as a picture of a whole life. Humility cannot be performed in a great sanctuary and left there. It goes where the feet go. If this is what God requires, the requirement reaches every street a person walks.

A question for you

Recall someone you know who walks humbly with God. What do they do that shows it?

Part 4 of 4

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوِ ٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ۚ إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا ۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ وَإِن تَلْوُۥٓا۟ أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allāh, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allāh is more worthy of both.[223] So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allāh is ever, of what you do, Aware.

Translator's notes

[223] i.e., more knowledgeable of their best interests. Therefore, adhere to what He has enjoined upon you and testify honestly.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:135

Translation

“‘You shall do no injustice in judgment. You shall not be partial to the poor, nor show favoritism to the great; but you shall judge your neighbor in righteousness.

Original · Hebrew

לֹא־תַעֲשׂ֥וּ עָ֨וֶל֙ בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט לֹא־תִשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי־דָ֔ל וְלֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר פְּנֵ֣י גָד֑וֹל בְּצֶ֖דֶק תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ט עֲמִיתֶֽךָ׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:15

World English Bible

A steward holds what belongs to another and answers for it. The verse asks for justice held firmly, as a witness for God, even against yourself, your parents and your kin. That is the test Micah pointed to. Justice costs something when it goes against your own. Whatever a people has been given, a sanctuary or a book, it was never meant to stand apart from this.

A question for you

What do you think the Temple was for?

If you sayTo bring God near to the people
ThenA beautiful answer, and the tradition gives it. Then what it was for has not gone. The question is how that nearness continues.
If you sayTo teach people to give up what they love
ThenThen it was a school of letting go. The hardest thing to give up, the verse suggests, is your own interest when it stands against what is right.
If you sayTo form a holy people who would act justly
ThenThen Micah's list is the fruit. The same question can be put to church, mosque and synagogue: what are they for?

The same in the other books

Translation

For the wisdom of the Lord is great. He is mighty in power, and sees all things. His eyes are upon those who fear him. He knows every act of man. He has not commanded any man to be ungodly. He has not given any man license to sin.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ὅτι πολλὴ σοφία τοῦ Κυρίου, ἰσχυρὸς ἐν δυναστείᾳ καὶ βλέπων τὰ πάντα. Καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς φοβουμένους αὐτὸν, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπιγνώσεται πᾶν ἔργον ἀνθρώπου. Καὶ οὐκ ἐνετείλατο οὐδενὶ ἀσεβεῖν, καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν ἄνεσιν οὐδενὶ ἁμαρτάνειν.

Sirach · 15:18-20

World English Bible

Translation

For you don’t delight in sacrifice, or else I would give it. You have no pleasure in burnt offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֤י ׀ לֹא־תַחְפֹּ֣ץ זֶ֣בַח וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה ע֝וֹלָ֗ה לֹ֣א תִרְצֶֽה׃ זִֽבְחֵ֣י אֱלֹהִים֮ ר֪וּחַ נִשְׁבָּ֫רָ֥ה לֵב־נִשְׁבָּ֥ר וְנִדְכֶּ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א תִבְזֶֽה׃

the Psalms · 51:16-17

World English Bible

Translation

“‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh. The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.

Original · Hebrew

לֹֽא־תִקֹּ֤ם וְלֹֽא־תִטֹּר֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְאָֽהַבְתָּ֥ לְרֵעֲךָ֖ כָּמ֑וֹךָ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃ כְּאֶזְרָ֣ח מִכֶּם֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם הַגֵּ֣ר ׀ הַגָּ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֗ם וְאָהַבְתָּ֥ לוֹ֙ כָּמ֔וֹךָ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:18, 34

World English Bible

Translation

“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
